entries.test: Whether Huang returns to lead NVIDIA, as documented by company announcements and filings.
entries.note: The context makes return as NVIDIA's leader the relevant outcome.
His assessment of Huang's entire value has no agreed factual measure.
The proposition removes 'perhaps' and substitutes NVIDIA for the bubble. 'Makes sense' supplies no shared test.

entries.test: Public investment, acquisition, guarantee and financing records showing whether NVIDIA's interventions enabled and increased AI spending.
Changes in ordinary investors' fund and retirement portfolio values attributable to a NVIDIA downturn.
entries.note: The preceding discussion of index exposure gives the metaphor a plain financial reading.
He presents manipulation as an impression: 'I feel like' and 'feels like.'

entries.test: Huang's public statements, deal documents and disclosed contemporaneous communications showing whether he knowingly misrepresented the deals' status.
entries.note: Documentary evidence can establish a specific allegation of commercial misrepresentation.

entries.test: Deal records, public announcements, disclosed communications and press coverage establishing whether the announcements deliberately misled markets and were amplified uncritically.

entries.note: The proposition weakens 'far more' to 'more.' There is no shared measure for ranking their foundational importance.

entries.test: Contemporaneous analyst reports, media coverage and financing or trading evidence showing their material contribution to NVIDIA and AI investment growth.
entries.note: 'I believe' introduces his asserted conclusion rather than an explicit probability.

entries.test: Contemporaneous business coverage and market commentary attributing revenue growth at NVIDIA customers to AI.
entries.note: The proposition changes 'basically any' into an unqualified 'any.'

entries.test: Stock-index performance attribution and company financial disclosures showing the market's dependence on AI and which businesses earned AI profits.
entries.note: 'Making money' has a plain profitability reading in this context.

entries.test: NVIDIA investment records and recipients' borrowing and GPU purchases showing whether its funding increased demand alongside its public demand claims.

entries.note: The drafter inserts 'meaningful.' The next sentence supplies actual AI revenue figures, making 'nowhere to be seen' an exaggeration.

entries.test: Order books, supply availability and customer financing records showing whether exceptional chip demand existed independently of NVIDIA's financing and pressure tactics.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives 'insatiable demand' a commercial reading of demand exceeding available supply.

entries.test: Customer inventory disclosures, warehouse records and purchase agreements establishing the value of uninstalled GPUs and the role of NVIDIA's purchasing pressure.
entries.note: 'I believe' states an evidence-based conclusion here; the drafter's 'likely' modality is not in the passage.

entries.test: Quarterly results, guidance and transaction records linking earnings beats and guidance increases to circular financing, smuggling and channel-stuffing.
The August analyst notes and industry revenue and compute-sales data showing the shares attributable to OpenAI and Anthropic buying compute.
entries.note: The proposition shifts an August finding to the present and omits that the revenue demand arose from their compute purchases.

entries.test: Customer financing and purchasing records showing whether demand attributed to NVIDIA was entirely generated by Huang's deals and NVIDIA's balance sheet.
entries.note: He rejects a substitution argument and asserts the demand's origin. He does not explicitly predict that AMD or Broadcom will capture none of it.
An actual collapse would not establish that every alternative course also required collapse.

entries.test: Export records, investigations, court filings and disclosed company communications establishing NVIDIA's involvement in prohibited GPU shipments to China.
Deal and revenue records alongside press coverage showing circular transactions increased NVIDIA revenue and whether coverage questioned those transactions.
entries.note: The proposition drops the categorical 'every single' and 'without any consideration' scope of the media allegation.
The claim explicitly extends to the counterfactual in which Huang returns or stays.

entries.test: AI financing, investment and valuation activity after Huang's departure showing whether the speculative boom continues without him.
entries.note: The article identifies the bubble with a financing-supported spending and valuation boom.
The proposition turns 'suggest' and 'a suggestion' into firm conclusions.

entries.test: Public financing and cash-flow records showing the remaining sources of support for AI businesses after Huang's departure and withdrawal of NVIDIA funding.
entries.note: The surrounding financing discussion supplies a plain reading of 'afloat.'

entries.test: A collapse in AI financing, spending and valuations following Huang's departure.
entries.note: No deadline is specified.

entries.test: Aggregate AI business revenues, costs and external financing flows showing whether the industry covers its costs or requires continued debt and venture funding.

entries.note: The asserted 'real reason' and what Huang cares about concern private motivation; transaction amounts alone cannot settle that.

entries.test: GPU purchasing, financing and customer decision records showing whether Huang's promotion and deals generated the claimed demand.
Dated financing cancellations, investment activity and market valuations showing whether the NVIDIA-supported boom collapsed within the week following Huang's departure.
entries.note: The surrounding passage supplies the departure as the temporal anchor.
The causal conclusion is expressly qualified by 'appears.'

entries.test: AI compute providers' sales and customer concentration data establishing the share sold to Anthropic and OpenAI.
entries.note: 'Most' weakens 'the vast majority.'

entries.test: Customer-level revenue concentration, customer financial results and NVIDIA investment records establishing the claimed concentration and funding relationships.
entries.note: The source says the largest purchasers are NVIDIA-funded, not that most of the concentrated customer group is NVIDIA-funded.

entries.test: Ramp's available quarterly spending data and Q4 tracking estimates showing whether growth was trending at 15–25% after 47% and over 140%.
entries.note: This reports a measurable current trend, not a firm prediction of the completed quarter.
'Bad deal' is an assessment of worth without a specified return criterion.
The proposition removes 'appears' from the revenue estimate. Its explanation for withholding disclosure asserts a private motive.

entries.test: OpenAI's Q3 2026 financial and fundraising disclosures and Microsoft's revenue breakdown showing losses, funds raised and growth excluding OpenAI.
entries.note: The proposition makes the Microsoft conclusion firm where the source says 'suggests.' The loss and fundraising figures are firm factual assertions.

entries.test: Neocloud financial statements showing profitability and loss margins, including those of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN.
Hyperscaler capacity, utilization and buildout disclosures alongside procurement records showing excess capacity and Huang's role in creating it.
AI startup revenue data, OpenAI and Anthropic financial statements and compute contracts establishing revenue share, losses and seven-year commitments requiring external funding.
entries.note: The source says most of the commitments depend on continued funding and debt; the proposition omits that limitation.

entries.test: Startup fundraising, revenue and expense disclosures and comparable GPU rental cost-per-output data showing funding dependence and customer efficiency trends.
entries.note: The proposition removes 'do not seem' and the stated fundraising cadence of every few months.
The possibility is explicitly introduced with 'may' and 'perhaps.'

entries.test: NVIDIA's subsequent financing guarantees and backing commitments showing whether businesses can still obtain its support.
entries.note: The proposition broadens a warning to those relying on theoretical backing into a categorical end to all future backstops.

entries.test: Representative willingness-to-pay surveys and AI compute customers' financial data establishing the prevalence of unwillingness to pay and inability to sustain compute costs.
entries.note: Both occurrences of 'most' weaken 'the vast majority.'

entries.test: NVIDIA's compute commitments, customer GPU purchases and compute utilization and sales records showing whether rent-backs compensate for substantially weaker end demand.

entries.note: 'All that anybody can think about' is hyperbole, not a measurable universal prediction.
